newsitem.title: UK: IMI Plc reports record full year profits.
newsitem.headline: IMI Plc reports record full year profits.

text.p: British engineering group IMI Plc announced record 1996 profits of 137.5 million pounds ($220.2 million) on Monday despite difficult trading conditions in mainland Europe.

"A profit improvement of 30 percent to a record level is confirmation of the success of our strategic thrust. Our gearing of 11 percent gives us ample scope for further growth," said chief executive Gary Allen. IMI was helped especially by the acquisition of Heimeier in 1995, maker of thermostat radiator valves, which contributed some 20 million pounds to profits.

IMI underwent a radical face lift last year, completing the acquisition of Heimeier in Germany and expanding through acquistition its drinks dispenser business. It enlarged its Fluid Power interests by buying ISI Automation, a U.S. manufacturer of pneumatic components for automated handling systems and sold almost all its titanium interests.
The company spent 239 million pounds ($382.4 million) on acquisitions in 1996 and realised a total 130 million from disposals, mainly from its titanium interests.
"The thrust of these changes has significantly strengthened our ability to compete globally and to continue profitable growth in IMI's chosen business areas," said Allen.

IMI said each of its business divisions performed well and added that trading so far in 1997 had been satisfactory. The company raised its total dividend to 13 pence per share up from 1.5p. IMI shares rose 5p to 369p in early trade as headline profits exceeded brokers forecast range of 131 to 137 million pounds. ($ = 0.625 British Pounds)
